_source.provenance: PLATFORM E7 conformance vectors - authored by the web client and transcribed here byte for byte. The 'payload' and 'web' members of every vector are theirs and were NOT computed by this app; the 'android' member is THIS app's observed behaviour, recorded beside theirs so a divergence cannot change silently in either direction.
_source.tick: 2026-08-23 coordinator tick: the platform's E7 security review found no phrase-exposure path and flagged the one gap no code review can close - their vectors and our scanner had never been run against each other. This file closes it.
_source.branch: task/1417 - PR #1451 [PARANOID-E7], NOT yet merged to origin/main as of this transcription
_source.outcomeVocabulary: Theirs: update-required | missing-mnemonic | missing-vault-id | invalid-mnemonic | invalid-vault-id | invalid-name | invalid-fingerprint. Ours: VaultQrRejection. The two vocabularies are deliberately different shapes, so 'agreement' compares the DECISION (accept/reject) and the parsed value, and names the cause difference separately.
_source.mnemonics: The public BIP-39 all-zero-entropy phrase (128 bits). Not a real phrase; opens no real vault.
_source.nameCap: The web caps `n` at 64 Unicode CODE POINTS ([...value].length); this app caps it at 64 UTF-16 CODE UNITS (String.length). Sec13 says '<= 64 chars'. See the maxLengthComposedName note.
_source.fingerprint: The web validates `f` against vaultKeyFingerprintSchema (base64url, exactly 16 chars) at parse time and rejects with invalid-fingerprint; this app carries any non-empty `f` verbatim because nothing offline can judge it and the comparison happens after the header fetch (Sec13 fetch-then-compare). Not exercised by their vectors - all of them carry a schema-valid 16-char fingerprint or none.

vectors.name: bareString
vectors.note: Both reject. The web collapses every non-`btvault1:` string into 'update-required'; this app splits it: a `btvault<n>:` prefix means UNSUPPORTED_VERSION ('update the app'), anything else means NOT_A_VAULT_CODE ('that is not a BetterTrack code'). Sec13's letter says 'anything else' gets the update notice; telling a user who scanned a Wi-Fi code to update the app is the reason this app diverged. Board question.

vectors.name: missingMnemonic
vectors.note: Same decision; this app's reason is one step coarser (it does not name WHICH required key is missing) because the UI collapses phrase-adjacent reasons anyway.

vectors.name: missingVaultId
vectors.note: Same decision, coarser reason - see missingMnemonic.

vectors.note: DIVERGENCE. The web rejects a repeated `m` (invalid-mnemonic). This app takes the FIRST value, like URLSearchParams.get(), and accepts. Sec13's letter is silent on repeated keys; its stated rationale ('parsed as one application/x-www-form-urlencoded query string, which every platform parses identically') points at reject, because duplicate keys are exactly where platform form parsers do NOT agree. Not changed unilaterally: silent in Sec13 -> board question.

vectors.note: Agrees for this vector only by luck of the alphabet: U+00E9 is one UTF-16 code unit, so the web's code-POINT cap and this app's code-UNIT cap coincide at 64. They part company on astral characters - 64 emoji is 64 code points (web accepts) and 128 code units (this app rejects NAME_TOO_LONG). Sec13 says '<= 64 chars' and settles nothing.
